A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
malignant epithelioid vascular neoplasms of the serous membrane are rare, but they should be considered in the differential diagnosis for patients with malignant mesotheliomas.
malignant epitheloid endothelial neoplastic lesions involving the serous cavities are rare but should be considered in the differential diagnosis for mesothelioma and adenocarcinomatous tumors.
malignant vascular tumors can be confused with mesothelioma because of the similar morphological features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when a patient has clinical features of malignant pleural mesothelioma but the histology is atypical, it is important to perform immunohistochemical stains for vimentin and the endothelial markers.

, in the setting of an aggressive mesothelioma with a diffuse, sheet-like pattern of tumor growth, a diagnosis of EHE/EA must be considered, and immunohistochemical staining for endothelial-associated markers may be useful in confirming the diagnosis of this rare entity.
, although rare, malignant vascular tumors of the pleura and peritoneum should be included in a differential diagnosis of mesothelioma.
